title: Distinguish transformer families, pretraining and adaptation, inference context, and sparse-expert routing without equating fluent output with verified reasoning

questions.prompt: A team needs a model that writes a short summary of each long support ticket. They are choosing between two pretrained checkpoints: **BERT** and **T5**. Explain why T5 can generate the summary text, while BERT on its own cannot. Base your answer on how each model is built.

rubric.point: BERT is encoder-only: it outputs contextual representations (one vector per token or a pooled vector) for a task head and has no autoregressive decoder to produce new tokens.
T5 is an encoder-decoder: the encoder reads the ticket, and the decoder generates the summary tokens one at a time (autoregressively) while attending to the encoder's output.

questions.model: BERT is encoder-only. It turns the input into contextual vectors for a task head, and it has no autoregressive decoder, so it cannot produce new text token by token. T5 is an encoder-decoder. Its encoder reads the ticket, and its decoder generates the summary one token at a time while attending to the encoder output.

questions.prompt: A GPT-style decoder-only model is pretrained on next-token prediction. After pretraining, the same stack can continue any prompt one token at a time. Which statement best explains why?
options: Its attention is bidirectional, so each position sees the whole sentence and can fill in whatever text is missing.
A causal mask lets each position attend only to earlier positions, so training to predict the next token matches how generation works.
Its very large parameter count stores enough text that it can recall a continuation for any prompt it is given.
Instruction fine-tuning after pretraining adds a separate decoder that turns the model's representations into text.

rubric.point: Selects the causal-mask explanation: each position predicts from earlier positions only, so next-token training matches token-by-token continuation.

questions.model: **B.** The causal mask means each position predicts only from earlier tokens. Training on next-token prediction therefore teaches exactly the step used at inference: append a token, then predict the next one.
